MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT
I. STATEMENT OF THE FACTS
Plaintiff initiated this foreclosure action against Alanda Ross and John B. Harris, AKA John Harris ("Defendants") and the real property commonly known as: 762 Bovee Lane, Powell, OH 43065 (the "Property").
On or about November 20, 2006, Alanda Ross and John B. Harris, AKA John Harris signed and delivered a promissory note (the "Note") in the original amount of $265,500.00. See Plaintiff's Affidavit attached hereto as an exhibit and a copy of the Note attached thereto.
To secure payment of the Note, Alanda Ross and John B. Harris, AKA John Harris signed and delivered a mortgage (the "Mortgage") on the Property. See Plaintiff's Affidavit and a copy of the recorded Mortgage attached thereto. The Mortgage remains a valid and subsisting lien on the Property, subject only to any lien that may be held by the County Treasurer that has priority over the Mortgage as a matter of law.
As established through Plaintiff's Affidavit and supporting evidence, Plaintiff is entitled not only to enforce the terms of the Note, but also the terms of the Mortgage, which was given to secure the Note. See Plaintiff's Affidavit. Defendants are in default of payment on the Note from February 1, 2014. See Plaintiff's Affidavit. As a result, Plaintiff has exercised its option to accelerate the balance due on the Note. The default remains uncured, and Defendants are in breach of the contract.
Defendant John B. Harris, AKA John Harris filed an Answer to Plaintiff's Complaint, which Answer contains no facts or defenses which could defeat summary judgment.
15-006289 MHF

II. LAW AND ARGUMENT
Summary judgment is appropriately rendered when there remains no genuine issue of material fact and, when construing the evidence most favorably towards the nonmoving party, reasonable minds could not draw different conclusions from the undisputed facts. Turner v. Turner, 67 Ohio St.3d 337, 341, 617 N.E.2d 1123 (1993). Under Civ.R. 56(C), the moving party bears the initial burden of identifying for the court the portions of the record that demonstrate the absence of a genuine issue of fact on a material element of the nonmoving party's claim.
Dresher v. Burt, 75 Ohio St.3d 280, 293, 662 N.E.2d 264 (1996). After the moving party has sufficiently supported the motion, the responding party may not rest upon the mere allegations and denials in the pleadings but must, instead, demonstrate with specificity that there exists a triable issue. Mitseff v. Wheeler, 38 Ohio St.3d 112, 115, 526 N.E.2d 798 (1988).
It is settled Ohio law that a default in payment under the terms of the promissory note entitles enforcement of the note once it has been accelerated. Gaul v. Olympia Fitness Center. Inc., 88 Ohio App.3d 310, 315, 623 N.E.2d 1281 (1993). Upon such a breach, the mortgagee may sue for foreclosure of the mortgage followed by sale of the mortgaged property. Levin v. Carney, 161 Ohio St. 513, 517-18, 120 N.E.2d 92 (1954).
Applying the foregoing standards to the facts of this case inarguably warrants the conclusion that Plaintiff must be granted judgment in its favor. There is no dispute that a material condition has been broken. See Plaintiff's Affidavit. Defendants agreed to make regular monthly mortgage payments until the entire principal amount and interest due under the Note were paid in full. See Plaintiff's Affidavit. Defendants failed to remit the requisite monthly

As a result, there is currently due and payable on the Note principal in the amount of $250,769.22, plus interest on the outstanding balance at the rate of 5.3% per annum from January 1, 2014, plus late charges and advances. See Plaintiff's Affidavit. By virtue of this default, Plaintiff is contractually entitled to foreclose the Property delivered as security under the Mortgage.

III. CONCLUSION
For the preceding reasons, Plaintiff respectfully requests that this Court grant summary judgment in its favor and find that Plaintiff is entitled to the relief prayed for in its pleadings. Plaintiff also requests an order granting it such other and further relief as this Court deems appropriate.
